text: Census records, Pompeii 78 CE: Population listed as 20,000 living residents, 3,847 not yet born. Vesuvius erupted the following year. All unborn citizens found in ash, fully formed.
Library circulation records, Alexandria 48 BCE: Final checkout before the fire was A Complete History of the Library of Alexandria by Marcus Didius. Book was due back in 52 BCE. Never returned.

Medical records, St. Bartholomew's Hospital 1665: Patient admitted with memories of plague he hasn't caught yet. Symptoms manifested three days before exposure. Recovery preceded infection by a fortnight.

Entry 1347A: Highway overpass constructed 1978 casts shadow of Roman aqueduct. Shadow functions as water channel during August thunderstorms. Engineering reports classify structure as functionally impossible, hydrologically sound.

Archaeological survey, Çatalhöyük 6500 BCE: Household shrine contains obsidian mirror reflecting rooms that won't be built for 8,000 years. Reflection shows electric lighting, running water. Mirror surface is authentically Neolithic.

Botanical survey, Kew Gardens 1889: Specimen labeled Quercus temporalis produces acorns that germinate into yesterday. Head gardener's notes mention chronological pruning required twice weekly to prevent causal loops.

Census records, Prague 1601: Household listed as containing two adults, three children, one Thursday. Thursday registered for tax purposes, attended local school, married in 1624. No surviving descendants.

Digital archive corruption, Library of Alexandria: Server logs from 48 CE show 404 errors for scrolls that won't be written until next century. Backup protocols reference magnetic tape storage. System administrator was a scribe named Marcus

Seismic survey, San Francisco 1906: Ground rupture patterns spell out apology letter in cursive script spanning 18 city blocks. Handwriting analysis matches penmanship of fault line itself. Geological formations rarely demonstrate remorse.

Radiographic analysis, Egyptian sarcophagus 1323 BCE: Xrays reveal mummy wrapped with newspapers from 1952. Headlines describe pharaoh's funeral in accurate detail. Papyrus authentically Dynasty XVIII, ink composition matches Chicago Tribun

Building permits, Toledo 1537: Cathedral extension approved for construction outside of time but within city limits. Foundation stones dated simultaneously to all centuries. Architect listed as The Department of Necessary Impossibilities.

Botanical survey, Amazon Basin: Tree ring analysis from 800yearold cecropia shows growth spurts during nuclear tests, 19451963. Tree predates European contact. Rings contain trace amounts of strontium90 from future atmospheric fallout.

Postal records, Morocco 1456: Letter delivered to recipient who died three years before sender was born. Postmark authenticated by guild of scribes. Reply was sent same day, arrived forty years early.

Census data, Northern England 1851: Household registry lists family of seven living in singleroom cottage with fourteen bedrooms. Enumerator's marginal note: Rooms exist only on Thursdays. Property tax assessed accordingly.

Archaeological excavation, Çatalhöyük 6500 BCE: Obsidian blade found with microscopic serial number etched in Latin script. Blade composition matches Anatolian volcanic glass. Serial format corresponds to 1970s manufacturing standards.
